note: The chart is arithmetic. Every coast vertex sits at one linear lon/lat mapping (x = 60 + (lon + 80) * 15.682, y = 520 - (lat - 36) * 17.143), both airports are where they really are, the arc is the quadratic through the true great-circle midpoint near 36W 51.5N, and the terminator sweeps WEST because that is the direction the real one moves. None of that was rebuilt for this film: it is the chart from showcase-flight.json with four token names changed and every clock re-timed. What changed is everything around it. The old film put that chart in a pale band under large black type on white paper, collided its own copy twice, and ended on a near-white card with the map thrown away. Here the map IS the frame, the sea is a backdrop that lightens as the terminator crosses it, and the film ends on the picture it spent twenty seconds building. The terminator's position is written once, in _flight-water.html, in the same form the chart's own terminator group uses, so the line you can see and the light it divides cannot drift apart. Plan and beat boundaries: formats/scene/showcase-flight-computed.storyboard.md.

audio._why: Shipped silent for this pass, and that is a gap rather than a decision. The film wants a low bed under the crossing that lifts as the light does, so the ear gets the same night-to-dawn ramp as the eye, and the storyboard says so. It is not here because the bed has not been chosen and cut, and a wrong one is worse than none. Not a claim that the film is better mute.

_cuts_why: THREE, not the seven beat boundaries, and all one family. A cut here is working against the film: the whole argument is that one object survives twenty seconds, and a transition is a moment where it does not. So they sit only at the three real turns (the crossing begins, the aircraft arrives, the camera pulls back) and every other beat boundary is carried by layers entering and leaving over a chart that never blinks. One family because three is the point at which docs/CRAFT/DIRECTION.md calls it effect soup, and the old film used five.
